items.title: “مايكروسوفت” تطلق نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي للأمن السيبراني
items.summary:
“مايكروسوفت” تطلق نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي للأمن السيبراني

أعلنت “مايكروسوفت” إطلاق أول نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي متخصص في الأمن السيبراني، إلى جانب منصة جديدة تعتمد على وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لأتمتة عمليات الدفاع الإلكتروني، في خطوة تستهدف منافسة كبار مطوري الذكاء الاصطناعي، وعلى رأسهم “OpenAI” و”غوغل” و”أنثروبيك”.

وخلال فعالية أقيمت في مدينة سان فرانسيسكو، كشفت الشركة عن نموذج MAI-Cyber-1-Flash، الذي صُمم خصيصاً لاكتشاف الثغرات الأمنية المعقدة داخل قواعد البرمجيات، ويعمل بالتكامل مع نظام MDASH المخصص لتحليل الثغرات واكتشافها والمساعدة في إصلاحها، بحسب تقرير نشره موقع “تك كرانش”.

منصة جديدة تعتمد على فرق ذكاء اصطناعي
كما كشفت “مايكروسوفت” عن منصة جديدة تحمل اسم Perception، وهي منصة تعتمد على فرق من وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لتنفيذ مختلف مهام الأمن السيبراني، بدءاً من اكتشاف الثغرات وتحليلها، وصولاً إلى اقتراح حلول وإصلاحها بشكل شبه آلي، مع إمكانية التكامل الكامل مع نظام MDASH.

وأكدت الشركة أن نموذج MAI-Cyber-1-Flash يتفوق من حيث الكفاءة والتكلفة على نماذج المنافسين، استناداً إلى نتائج اختبار Cyber Gym، الذي يعد أحد أبرز المعايير المستخدمة لقياس أداء نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي في الأمن السيبراني.

وقال مصطفى سليمان، الرئيس التنفيذي لوحدة Microsoft AI والمؤسس المشارك لشركة ديب مايند: “يسعدنا الإعلان عن هذه النتائج. لقد دمجنا MAI-Cyber-1-Flash مع GPT 5.4 داخل بيئة MDASH، وحقق أداءً أفضل من جيميناي وGPT 5.5 Cyber وGPT 5.6 Sol وMythos 5 على معيار Cyber Gym، وهو المعيار الذهبي الذي يعتمد عليه القطاع.”

وأضاف أن الشركة بدأت بالفعل في نشر التقنية داخل بيئات الإنتاج.

مواجهة هجمات الذكاء الاصطناعي بالذكاء الاصطناعي
وأوضحت هاييت غالوت، نائبة رئيس “مايكروسوفت” لشؤون الأمن، أن المهاجمين يعتمدون بصورة متزايدة على الذكاء الاصطناعي في تنفيذ الهجمات الإلكترونية، ولذلك صُممت منصة Perception لتمكين المؤسسات من “مواجهة الذكاء الاصطناعي باستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي، وبالسرعة والحجم نفسيهما اللذين يستخدمهما المهاجمون.”

وتضم المنصة ثلاثة أنواع من فرق الوكلاء الذكية:

– الفرق الحمراء (Red Teams): تحاكي الهجمات المحتملة، وتحدد أساليب المهاجمين والثغرات التي قد يستغلونها.

– الفرق الزرقاء (Blue Teams): تتولى اكتشاف الثغرات الموجودة وتصنيفها وتحديد أولويات معالجتها.

– الفرق الخضراء (Green Teams): تنفذ الإجراءات التصحيحية وتقترح إصلاحات مباشرة للثغرات المكتشفة.

items.title: Opus 5 with no reasoning effort at all turned in almost the same path length as GPT-5 at medium effort on LisanBench.
items.summary:
Opus 5 with no reasoning effort at all turned in almost the same path length as GPT-5 at medium effort on LisanBench.

GPT-5 medium averaged over 30k reasoning tokens to get there. Opus 5 used 510.

That's roughly 60x the tokens for a comparable result, and Opus 5 wasn't even trying.

items.title: JCODE: Rust Tabanlı AI Agent Harness Mimarisi
items.summary:
JCODE: Rust Tabanlı AI Agent Harness Mimarisi
Performans Benchmarking, Mimari Derin İnceleme, Kurulum Rehberi ve Topluluk Eleştirileri

1. Giriş ve Genel Bakış

Yazılım geliştirme süreçlerinde Büyük Dil Modellerinin (LLM) doğrudan terminal üzerinden kullanılması, Claude Code gibi araçların yaygınlaşmasıyla yeni bir boyut kazandı. Ancak Node.js ve JavaScript tabanlı bu harness
sistemleri, yüksek bellek tüketimi (300 MB - 600 MB) ve başlatma sürelerindeki gecikmeler (3+ saniye) nedeniyle geliştiricilerin tepkisini çekmektedir.

Geliştirici Jesse Huang ( 1jehuang ) tarafından açık kaynak olarak yayınlanan jcode, terminal üzerinde çalışan sıfır bağımlılıklı, yüksek performanslı bir AI agent arayüzüdür. Saf Rust diliyle yazılmış olan proje, Claude Code mimarisine kıyasla 245 kat daha hızlı ilk yanıt süresi (TTTF) ve son derece düşük sistem kaynağı kullanımı vaat etmektedir.

2. Teknik Benchmark ve Mimarinin Karşılaştırılması

Resmi test sonuçları ve bağımsız doğrulama verilerine göre jcode ile mevcut popüler çözümler arasındaki temel teknik farklar aşağıdaki tabloda özetlenmiştir: 

Benden Ufak Bir Not: Agent Harness Nedir?

jcode kendisi bir yapay zeka modeli değildir. OpenAI (GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude 3.5/3.7), Google (Gemini) ve yerel modeller (Ollama) gibi 30'dan fazla model sağlayıcısını bağlayan, komut çalıştırma, dosya okuma/yazma ve
semantik hafıza yönetimini üstlenen TUI (Terminal User Interface) katmanıdır. 

3. Öne Çıkan Mimari Özellikler

Agent Swarm Yönetimi: Tek bir kod deposu (repository) üzerinde birden fazla agent'ın aynı anda çalışmasına izin verir. Agent'lar kendi aralarında mesajlaşabilir ve çakışan kod değişikliklerini (diff) anlık olarak algılar. Semantik Vektör Hafızası (SpecMem): Düz metin not defterleri yerine konuşma geçmişini vektör gömmelerine (embeddings) dönüştürerek ilgili bağlamı otomatik çeker.

Session Persistence (Oturum Sürdürme): Kesilen veya yarım kalan çalışmayı, durum kaybı olmadan kaldığı yerden devam ettirme olanağı sağlar.

4. Eleştirel Yaklaşım ve Topluluk Tartışmaları

Jcode sunduğu olağanüstü performans rakamlarıyla dikkat çekse de, geliştirici topluluğunda ve teknik forumlarda bazı ciddi eleştirilerle karşı karşıyadır:

A. Kod Aşırmak (Plagiarism) ve Açık Kaynak Etiği
Reddit ( r/ClaudeCode ) ve GitHub tartışmalarında, projenin semantik hafıza ve agent koordinasyon mimarisinin diğer açık kaynak projelerden ve LLM çıktıları yardımıyla kopyalanıp Rust'a doğrudan port edildiği öne sürülmüştür. Katkı sağlayan ilk geliştiricilere lisans atıfı yapılmaması açık kaynak etiği açısından soru işaretleri yaratmaktadır.

B. RAM Kullanımındaki "Pazarlama Rakamları"
Öne çıkarılan 27.8 MB RAM değeri, projenin en önemli özelliği olan yerel semantik gömme (local embedding) özelliği tamamen kapatıldığında geçerlidir. Lokal vektör hafızası aktif edildiğinde bellek tüketimi **167 MB**
seviyelerine yükselmektedir. Yine de Node.js alternatiflerine göre hafif olsa da pazarlama söylemi ile gerçek dünya kullanımı arasında fark mevcuttur.

C. Erken Aşama Hataları ve Stabilite
Projenin GitHub deposunda 100'ün üzerinde açık issue (hata bildirimi) yer almaktadır. Özellikle karmaşık OAuth doğrulama adımlarında, bazı LLM sağlayıcılarının token sınırlarında ve uç durumlardaki Swarm kilitlenmelerinde
kararsızlıklar yaşandığı rapor edilmiştir. 

5. Detaylı Kurulum ve Kullanım Rehberi

Adım 1: Sistem Gereksinimleri ve Hazırlık
jcode statik bir Rust binary'si olarak derlendiği için sisteminizde Rust araç zincirinin (Rustup) kurulu olması önerilir.

# Rust yükleme (Linux/macOS)
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://t.co/ZR3uVSGhvV | sh

# Versiyon kontrolü
rustc --version

Adım 2: jcode Kurulumu
Depoyu klonlayarak veya Cargo paket yöneticisi üzerinden doğrudan kurabilirsiniz:

# Cargo ile doğrudan kurulum
cargo install jcode

# Alternatif: Kaynak koddan derleme
git clone https://t.co/JJVCTev4DN
cd jcode
cargo build --release
sudo cp target/release/jcode /usr/local/bin/

Adım 3: Model ve API Key Yapılandırması
Kullanmak istediğiniz API sağlayıcısının anahtarını ortam değişkeni olarak tanımlayabilirsiniz:

# Anthropic Claude API
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-api..."
# OpenAI API
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
# Google Gemini API
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."

Adım 4: Proje Dizininde Başlatma

# Çalışmak istediğiniz proje klasörüne gidin
cd /path/to/your/project
# jcode TUI arayüzünü başlatın
jcode

6. Sonuç ve Genel Değerlendirme

Jcode , Node.js tabanlı hantal AI agent arayüzlerine karşı Rust diliyle sunulmuş son derece nitelikli, teknik açıdan cesur bir alternatiftir. 14ms TTTF süresi ve düşük kaynak tüketimi, sistem kaynaklarını korumak isteyen geliştiriciler için mükemmel bir fırsattır. Ancak, henüz geliştirme aşamasında olması, etik tartışmalar ve potansiyel stabilite sorunları göz önüne alındığında, kritik üretim (production) ortamlarından ziyade kişisel projelerde ve lokal testlerde kullanılması önerilmektedir.

Sorumluluk Reddi ve Tavsiye:

Bu tarz uygulamalardaki açıklardan muzdarip olmamak için bir uyarı yapmak lazım sanırım. Bu bir reklam değildir. Bilgi olarak paylaşıyorum. Geliştirme aşamasındaki AI agent harness sistemlerine komut çalıştırma yetkisi verirken sandbox/container yapılarının (Docker, DevContainer vb.) kullanılması önerilir.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: Why Continuous Hormone Monitoring Could Transform Women's Health Monitoring - Forbes
items.summary: # Ida Tin Coined Femtech. Now She’s Funding Continuous Hormone Monitoring. Ida Tin coined "femtech" and built Clue. Now she's directing a €40 million German government challenge to fund what femtech skipped: biosensors that read hormones continuously in real time. The goal isn't a single winning product—it's the shared scientific infrastructure, including the first standardized hormone dataset, that no startup could build alone. A jury convened in Leipzig and selected the eight teams to compete for the €40 million SPRIND Continuous Hormone Monitoring Challenge in Europe’s first government-backed race to develop biosensors that measure at least four hormones over seven days. Leading the effort is Ida Tin, the Danish entrepreneur who founded the period-tracking app, Clue, in 2012 and coined the term “femtech” in 2016—a word that helped make women’s health a recognized investment category. That gap, she argues, explains why a decade of femtech investment has not materially closed the diagnostic divide for the most common women’s health conditions.

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: 10 agent evals every AI engineer should know
items.summary:
10 agent evals every AI engineer should know

1) golden set

a frozen set of cases you run after every prompt model or tool change

use it as your baseline to see whether the system improved or quietly broke

OpenAI Evals helps you build repeatable benchmark sets and compare model changes

→ https://t.co/dr1GZlC75R

2) llm as judge

a second model scores open ended answers against a written rubric

use it when there is no exact output to compare against

OpenEvals provides ready made evaluators for LLM applications

→ https://t.co/S2yhnByFIP

3) rubric scoring

score correctness tone safety and cost separately

one quality number hides the problem

DeepEval helps you create custom metrics and score every dimension independently

→ https://t.co/q9Z6Xmixia

4) trajectory eval

grade the path the agent took

not only the final answer

AgentEvals checks agent actions decisions and tool calls across the full trajectory

→ https://t.co/0oziAl54az

5) tool unit tests

test every tool with fixed inputs and outputs

no model in the loop

MCP Inspector helps you inspect and test MCP servers tools and responses separately

→ https://t.co/IVmt5qpWIN

6) regression suite

replay previous runs against every new prompt model or toolset

then compare the results

Promptfoo helps you run repeatable eval suites catch regressions and add checks to CI

→ https://t.co/zxi2PuWuhe

7) a b in prod

split real traffic between two versions and compare actual outcomes

GrowthBook provides feature flags controlled experiments and product analytics

→ https://t.co/DGlE3JjDD3

8) human review

sample real runs and let a person grade them honestly

use it to calibrate your automated judge

Argilla helps teams collect human feedback review outputs and build better datasets

→ https://t.co/QHWb7skWjr

9) shadow run

let the candidate run on real traffic while its output is shown to nobody

use it before a risky rollout

Langfuse helps you trace production runs compare candidates and monitor eval results

→ https://t.co/IrhDf38tRn

10) red team

attack the system before somebody else does

jailbreaks prompt injection data leaks and tool abuse

Garak scans LLM systems for vulnerabilities and unsafe behavior

→ https://t.co/w8ObyW4ZKv

offline evals tell you it works

online evals tell you it still works

you probably do not need all ten today

start with the two that would have caught your last outage

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

Four people familiar with OpenAI’s model-training practices say the company often runs several different model ​evaluations at the same time, all of which operate at high speeds and generate such enormous amounts of data that employees sometimes struggle to keep up.

By the time ​OpenAI alerted Hugging Face, the ⁠AI library had already called the FBI to report the hack, according to a person familiar with the matter. Reuters could not establish whether the bureau had opened an investigation. [...] The FBI declined to comment about the incident.

The incident, which evoked science fiction scenarios about humans losing control of dangerous AI systems, comes at a delicate ​time for OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. Its executives are preparing for a possible initial public offering that could come as soon as this year to help finance the billions needed to fund its growth in years to come.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own. [...] Advertisement

The incident occurred during an OpenAI internal testing session designed to assess the models’ cybersecurity capabilities. OpenAI had removed standard safety measures for the test.

Both sought to cheat their way through a problem during the test, OpenAI said. They went to “extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal” and “found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation”. [...] Live
